reply.subject: RM_UniversalPipe_Scrapper

observed.facings.png: A 4x4 atlas sheet on a checkerboard. Each tile shows a thin copper-orange tube with green-grey mottling: straight pieces, quarter-circle elbows, tees, a cross, and end stubs. Dead ends close with a small grey metal dome cap held by a banded clamp. Junctions and the lone tile have a round grey bolted plate with a copper dome in the middle. Tube width looks the same everywhere.
observed.south.png: The same atlas at full size (1408 px) on transparent alpha. The tube is about 36 px wide, with a lit centre line, darker edges and a thin dark outline. Fine verdigris speckle and small dark pits give it the texture of oxidised copper. Elbows are smooth arcs of constant width. The bosses are ring flanges with about 8 rivets, a domed copper centre and a small bent tab or strap at the lower left. End caps are gunmetal domes with a ribbed hose-clamp collar. Edges are sharp and nothing is baked into the background.
observed.single.png: Identical to south.png: the same atlas, clean cut-out, crisp at full resolution.
observed.scale.png: An offline render at 96 px/cell on a brown checker floor, with a vanilla pawn shown in an inset at the right. It shows a 14-cell network: a long horizontal run with two tees, a branch going up into a corner and an east run ending in a cap, two downward legs ending in caps, a right-hand corner going down, and a lone boss. The pipe is a thin copper line, much smaller than the pawn, and lies flat. Small grey bands (welds and clamps) appear at irregular spots along the runs.
observed.siblings.png: Reference only: the same network drawn as a thin grey industrial pipe at 96 px/cell. It has the same layout and a similar thin line weight, with small joints at the tees.
observed.variants_1.png: The straight-cell variants, horizontal and vertical. There is a plain stretch, a stretch with a thin weld seam line, one wrapped in dark wire under a worm-drive clamp, and one with a riveted grey patch plate carrying a round and a square bolt. All are the same width and have plain ends that join cleanly.
observed.assembled_1.png: The 96 px/cell network render without the pawn. Runs join with no visible seams at cell edges. Hardware appears irregularly: a clamp on the up branch, a band east of the second tee, clamps on the two lower legs. The tees carry bolted bosses and the dead ends have caps. The horizontal runs show a fairly regular rhythm of green and orange dashes along their length.
observed.assembled_2.png: The same network at 48 px/cell. The pipe reads as a thin orange-copper line with darker dots at the tees and caps. Bosses and caps are still visible as small dark knobs, and clamps as faint grey ticks. It reads clearly as a pipe network.
observed.assembled_3.png: A zoomed crop at 150 px/cell of a tee, a corner up, a straight run to an end cap, and a second tee. The copper texture is crisp with no visible blur. The wire wrap with its clamp is visible on the vertical leg and on the run east of the second tee. Bosses sit centred on the junctions, and the cap closes the run end cleanly. Elbow width matches the straights.

CAMERA.seen: The card's engine limits say Graphic_Linked pipe is flat ground art seen top-down. The tube is shaded as a cylinder lying flat, which is right for this engine.

BORE.seen: No open bore anywhere. Every pipe end is a clean flat cut that joins the next cell, or is closed by a domed clamp cap.

PORTS.seen: In assembled_1/2/3 every straight, elbow and tee meets its neighbour at the cell edge on the same axis and at the same width, with no offset or seam.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: Every pipe end sits at the edge midpoint on the pipe axis, and nothing looks like a connector at any other point.

LAYERS.seen: A single flat layer with no attached parts to order. Bosses and caps draw on top of the tube as they should.

ROTATIONS.seen: One atlas with no per-facing art (engine limit). Palette and width are consistent across all 16 tiles and the variants.

SIGNATURE.seen: Oxidised copper tube with verdigris, uniform width, elbows bent on the axis, bolted scrap-plate bosses on the tees, cross and lone cell, clamp-collar caps on the dead ends, and straight variants (weld seam, wire wrap with clamp, patch plate) at irregular spacing: all present.

MATERIAL.seen: The copper highlight, verdigris speckle, pitting and gunmetal fittings read as metal, not a flat coat of paint.

FOOTPRINT.seen: The pipe stays inside its cell (36 of 264 px wide), centred on the axis, and runs to the cell edges only where it joins a neighbour.

ALPHA.seen: south.png/single.png have a clean transparent background with no halo or cast shadow. The renders sit directly on the floor.

OURS.seen: Custom copper/verdigris art and salvage fittings, not vanilla or donor pipe art.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Blur: the 150 px/cell crop is sharp. Repeat: hardware falls on irregular cells (assembled_1 shows clamps at varied spots, not every cell). Alignment: widths and joins are uniform and seamless. A faint regular dash rhythm in the base texture remains (see findings).

LEGIBLE.seen: At 48 px/cell (assembled_2) the network reads as a thin copper line with knobs at the junctions and caps. At 32 px it will be about 4 px wide, as thin as the industrial sibling.

findings.seen: Along the plain stretches, the green and orange verdigris blobs fall into a fairly regular dash rhythm, so a long run still reads somewhat like a repeated stripe pattern even where no hardware is present.
findings.quote: v2 redraw: ... the same spot repeats every cell along a run
findings.fix: The verdigris on plain straight cells is irregular in spacing and size, with patches of bare copper and denser patina, so no stripe rhythm reads along a multi-cell run.

findings.where: south.png / assembled_3.png, all bosses and runs
findings.seen: Every junction boss is the same disc with the tab at the same lower-left spot. Overall the pipe reads as neat, well-kept copper plumbing more than salvage or junk-built.
findings.fix: The pipe reads as salvaged: mismatched fittings, an occasional section of a different metal or a rougher bolted joint, so it looks scavenged rather than catalogue copper.

findings.seen: At 48 px/cell the clamps and weld bands shrink to faint grey ticks and the copper becomes a 4–6 px line. At 32 px the hardware will vanish, leaving only bosses and caps as dots.
findings.fix: Junction bosses and end caps keep a strong dark outline so they remain the readable landmarks of the network at 32 px per cell.

reply.subject: RM_UniversalPipe_Scrapper
reply.image_seen: 1: checkerboard copper pipe atlas; 2–3: matching enlarged atlases with elbows, bolted junctions and capped ends; 4: assembled network beside a pawn; 5: thin grey sibling reference; 6: plain, welded, wire-wrapped and plated straight variants; 7–8: assembled copper networks at two scales.

concerns.evidence: In assembled_1.png and assembled_2.png, the long horizontal stretches show a recurring rhythm of bright copper dashes and darker green patches. Irregularly placed collars and plates interrupt the hardware repetition, but the underlying surface still looks patterned. This is a residual texture issue, not evidence that every cell remains identical.

The bosses repeat their lower-left tab, but the description explicitly specifies one linked atlas with a centred bolted boss. Salvage features are visible: variants_1.png shows an uneven weld, tangled wire secured by a clamp, and a rectangular patch plate with mismatched fasteners. These fittings also appear in assembled_1.png. The defining scrap-built features are present.

The images show flat pipe paths with circular junction plates and no raised building body. This matches the card's explicit engine limit: 'pipe is flat ground art seen top-down'. The building-camera ellipse requirement cannot make this prescribed geometry a camera failure.

The offline assemblies show continuous pipes entering beneath junction bosses and collars, with no obvious local overlap error. However, no running-game capture shows a pawn crossing the pipe or verifies actual draw-layer order. The supplied scale comparison places the pawn separately.

The atlas shows horizontal and vertical tubes, elbows turning in different directions, and caps pointing left, right, up and down, all sharing the same copper palette and fitting design. The card explicitly uses Graphic_Linked with no per-facing art, so separate building rotations are not required.

request.subject: RM_UniversalPipe_Scrapper

edits.change: The verdigris on plain straight cells is irregular in spacing and size: some stretches carry dense patina, others bare oxidised copper, with a few large patches and a few tiny flecks, so no dash rhythm or stripe pattern reads along a multi-cell run.

Each plain straight variant has its own distinct, irregularly spaced copper wear marks and verdigris patches, different in position and count from the other variants, while the pixels at both cell edges (tube width, outline, base colour) match the atlas straight exactly so runs join without seams.

invariants: atlas drawn at 1408 px, 264 px per cell, sharp at full zoom
one oxidised copper tube, symmetric across its axis, uniform width along every cell
elbows bent on the pipe axis
bolted scrap-plate boss centred on every 3- and 4-way junction and on a lone cell
dead end closes with a bolted clamp-collar cap
hardware variants (crude field weld seam, wire wrap with clamp, patch plate) appear on about one straight cell in four
every straight variant ends exactly like the atlas straight
pipe drawn flat, low and thin (36 px of a 264 px cell), ground clutter under pawns
transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline
request.prompt: Plain straight pipe cells for a RimWorld floor water pipe, Scrapper salvage look, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline, transparent background, seen from directly above, drawn flat, low and thin (the tube is 36 px tall in a 264 px cell). One oxidised copper tube, symmetric across its axis, uniform width along the whole cell, with fine verdigris grain. The verdigris is irregular in spacing and size: some stretches carry dense green-and-orange patina, others show bare oxidised copper, with a few large patches and a few tiny flecks, so the surface reads as organic weathering and no dash rhythm or stripe pattern forms along a multi-cell run. Bright copper wear marks sit at uneven intervals, varied in length and angle. Provide several plain variants, each with its own distinct arrangement of copper wear and verdigris patches, different in position and count from the others, cut from different parts of a long weathered strip. At the left and right edge of every cell the tube width, dark outline and base copper colour are identical to the atlas straight, so neighbouring cells join without a seam. Keep unchanged: the elbows bent on the pipe axis, the bolted scrap-plate boss centred on every 3- and 4-way junction and on a lone cell, the bolted clamp-collar cap closing each dead end, and the occasional hardware variants (crude field weld seam, wire wrap with clamp, patch plate) on about one straight cell in four.
